reasoning.step1:
1) Classify document:
- Contains clear invoice indicators: title "Rechnung", "Nummer", "Datum", totals ("Gesamtbetrag", "Zahlbetrag"), VAT lines. No exclusion terms (e.g., "Mahnung") dominate. Conclusion: document is an invoice.

2) Locate candidate fields:
- Invoice date: line "Datum 26.01.2024" appears top of page.
- Grand total / payable: "Zahlbetrag 47,16 EUR".
- Net amount: "Gesamtbetrag Netto 40,43 EUR".
- VAT rate and VAT amount: "R2 - 20,00% USt auf 40,43 ... 8,09 EUR" and "20.00%" formatting appears as "20.00%"/ "20,00%" (OCR shows "20.00%"/"20,00%"); VAT amount shown as "8,09 EUR".
- Sender VAT ID: two VAT IDs appear:
  - "Ihre Ust-Id-Nr. ATU64131246" (appears in header as "Ihre" — refers to customer).
  - Footer shows "Ust.-ID-Nr. ATU69710958" with company CREATON info — this matches sender. Per schema, Sender.VatId should be sender's VAT -> ATU69710958.

3) Verify formats and no inference:
- Use exact numeric values from document, preserving decimals.
- Convert comma decimals to dot for JSON numeric fields.
- VAT rate: document shows 20.00% / 20,00% — extract numeric 20.00 (no percent symbol) and preserve two decimal places as in source.
- Do not infer any missing fields.

4) Map to schema:
- GrandTotal.Amount -> Zahlbetrag 47,16 => 47.16
- Invoice.Date -> "26.01.2024" (string)
- Sender.VatId -> sender VAT in footer "ATU69710958"
- Vat.Rate -> 20.00 (from "20.00%"/"20,00%")
- Net.Amount -> 40,43 => 40.43
- Vat.Amount -> 8,09 => 8.09

5) Confirm no conflicting multiple occurrences:
- Only one invoice date and one Zahlbetrag visible.
- Two VAT IDs present; selected the sender's (CREATON) per context in footer.
- VAT group corresponds to entire invoice (R2 line applies to Gesamtbetrag Netto), so include it.

6) Ready to produce final JSON with those extracted values.
